question.worked_solution:
Given two $n\times n$ matrices $M$ and $N,$ we have

$$
det(MN)=det(M)\cdot det(N).
$$

In our case, this gives

$$
det(A)=det[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot det[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

We can compute the required determinants as follows:

- For the first determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion down the $2$nd column.

- For the second determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion across the $3$rd row.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|\cdot 2(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(1-2)\cdot 2(1+2) \\  & =1\cdot 6 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
